newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish groups slam Denmark's barring of Rushdie.
newsitem.headline: Swedish groups slam Denmark's barring of Rushdie.

text.p: Denmark's decision to bar British author Salman Rushdie from collecting a European Union (EU) literary prize in person was strongly criticised by Swedish literary groups on Friday.
"To give out the EU prize in a European Cultural Capital and then not allow Rushdie in (to the country) is scandalous," chairwoman of Sweden's PEN club, Monica Nagler, told Swedish news agency TT.

Denmark said on Thursday Rushdie would not be allowed to collect his prize in person, citing security concerns because of advance publicity as well as pressure on police resources from a Nordic biker gang war.
"The visit this time is known about in advance and we use so many resources to keep an eye on the bikers," Copenhagen police chief Hanne Bech Hansen said.
Arne Ruth, chairman of the Swedish Rushdie Committee, said it was an outrage that Rushdie, a British citizen, should be barred from another EU country.
"He has the right to move freely throughout the EU," Ruth told TT.
"I have not heard of a more obvious breach of human rights in the EU. Denmark's decision is a victory for the Iranians who are behind the death threat on Rushdie."
Nagler said the committee would send a letter of protest to the Danish government.

Rushdie has lived in hiding and with permanent protection since 1989, when Iranian revolutionary leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini issued a death threat, in the form of an Islamic decree or "fatwa", against him for his novel "The Satanic Verses".
Presentation of the literary awards for Rushdie's work as well as to Austrian writer Christoph Ransmayer and Danish author and translator Thorkild Bjoernvig is scheduled for November 14.
